```console
"""Per-target bias with R = 100 subset draws against the R = 10 main run: does Table 3's bias^2 / variance split change?

usage: python3 -I scripts/14_bias_r100.py results/highR/per_bench.csv.gz results/per_bench.csv.gz results/highR_vs_main.csv results/raw_highR/target_level.parquet results/highR_target_bias.csv

Both inputs are 03_analyze.py outputs. For n = 100, the non-thin benchmarks and the methods present in both (the R = 100 run has the designs uniform, strat, pps, balanced
only, splits interp and extrap), per (split, method): the mean over benchmarks of bias2_unbiased, var and MSE (= rmse^2), each divided by the MSE of uniform|mean of the same
run and benchmark (as in Table 3), for R = 10 and R = 100, with the standard error over benchmarks of the R = 100 mean. bias2_unbiased = bias^2 of the draw-mean error minus
var/R, so it does not contain the Monte-Carlo variance of the draw mean; at R = 10 that correction is up to 10 % of the MSE, at R = 100 up to 1 %.
"""
import sys, pathlib, numpy as np, pandas as pd
hi, lo, out, tl, out2 = sys.argv[1:6]
rows = []
for tag, f in (("R10", lo), ("R100", hi)):
    pb = pd.read_csv(f); pb = pb[(pb.n == 100) & (~pb.thin) & (~pb.method.str.contains("fixed:")) & pb.split.isin(["interp", "extrap"])]
    mu = (pb.rmse / pb.ratio) ** 2
    pb = pb.assign(b2=pb.bias2_unbiased / mu, v=pb["var"] / mu, mse=pb.ratio ** 2, run=tag)
    rows.append(pb[["run", "bench", "split", "method", "b2", "v", "mse"]])
d = pd.concat(rows)
common = set(d[d.run == "R100"].method) & set(d[d.run == "R10"].method)
d = d[d.method.isin(common)]
g = d.groupby(["split", "method", "run"])[["b2", "v", "mse"]].agg(["mean", lambda x: x.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x))])
g.columns = [f"{a}_{'mean' if b == 'mean' else 'se'}" for a, b in g.columns]
w = g.reset_index().pivot(index=["split", "method"], columns="run")
w.columns = [f"{a}_{b}" for a, b in w.columns]
for c in ("b2", "v", "mse"):
    w[f"{c}_diff"] = w[f"{c}_mean_R100"] - w[f"{c}_mean_R10"]
w = w.reset_index(); w.to_csv(out, index=False)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
print(w[["split", "method", "b2_mean_R10", "b2_mean_R100", "b2_se_R100", "v_mean_R10", "v_mean_R100", "mse_mean_R10", "mse_mean_R100"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("benchmarks:", d.groupby("run").bench.nunique().to_dict())

# Per-target signed bias of the R = 100 draw mean against its Monte-Carlo standard error sqrt(draw_var / n_draws): pooled over the targets of the non-thin benchmarks.
t = pd.read_parquet(tl); t = t[t.n == 100]
thin = pd.read_csv(str(pathlib.Path(hi).parent / "targets.csv")); thin = set(map(tuple, thin[thin.thin][["bench", "split"]].values))
t = t[[(b, s) not in thin for b, s in zip(t.bench, t.split)]]
t = t.assign(method=t.design + "|" + t.estimator, se=np.sqrt(t.draw_var / t.n_draws))
r = t.groupby(["split", "method"]).apply(lambda g: pd.Series(dict(
    n_targets=len(g), median_abs_bias=g.bias.abs().median(), median_mc_se=g.se.median(), share_abs_bias_gt_2se=(g.bias.abs() > 2 * g.se).mean(),
    share_bias2_of_mse=((g.bias ** 2 - g.se ** 2).sum() / g.sq_err.sum())))).reset_index()
r.to_csv(out2, index=False)
print(r[r.method.isin(["uniform|mean", "uniform|irt-model", "uniform|diff-irt", "balanced|diff-irt", "uniform|calreg", "uniform|ridge-model"])].round(3).to_string(index=False))
```

I approved `paper-repo` PR #7 at head `b44a3af`, so it can merge into `release`.

- **Page limit:** the main text now ends on page 9, with the References after it. The PDF is 29 pages.
- **Broken reference:** `\ref{fig:msrc}` is restored. The PDF text has no `effig`, `??` or raw labels left.
- **R = 100 check in Section 5.2:** it matches `code/results/highR_vs_main.csv`, with the squared bias of the IRT model in extrapolation going from 4.29 to 4.42. The script and results are shipped.

One minor point is not blocking. Section 5.2 says no entry changes by more than 0.13, but the largest difference in the CSV is 0.137 (extrapolation, balanced design, kNN plug-in). The paper should say 0.14, or name which methods the sentence covers.

For `final`, M6 and M7 are still open. M6 is the public-baseline result, whose script is shipped but whose result isn't in the paper. M7 is the recalibrated estimator, or a statement of what was attempted.

The review record is `reviews/v1-paper-repo-pr7-head-b44a3af.md`, pushed to internal-review-repo.
